literal: Fearing the inner trembling of those whose refuge is small, if their objective is obtained, the great will accept it, bowing humbly.
translation: Fearing the inner terror of those with weak defenses, great leaders will accept their objective and make peace, even by acting with humility.
modern: பாதுகாப்பு குறைந்த எளியவர்கள் மனநடுங்குவதை அஞ்சி, தங்களுக்கு வேண்டிய காரியம் நிறைவேறினால், பெரியவர்கள் பணிவுடன் நடந்து அதை ஏற்றுக் கொள்வார்கள்.
explanation: This couplet explains the strategic humility of great leaders when dealing with weaker adversaries. Great statesmen do not seek to utterly terrify or destroy those who have weak defenses ('uṟai ciṟiyār'). Fearing the inner trembling ('uḷ naṭuṅkal añci') that extreme terror might cause in the weak—which could drive them to desperate, unpredictable actions—the great will gladly accept their objective ('kuṟai peṟiṉ') and conclude the matter, even by humbling themselves ('paṇintu koḷvar') to ensure a peaceful resolution.
